newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish shares rise 1.73 pct in lower volume.
newsitem.headline: Turkish shares rise 1.73 pct in lower volume.

text.p: Istanbul shares extended gains on Thursday after parliament rejected sending Deputy Prime Minister Tansu Ciller to the Supreme Court in three corruption charge votes in the past two days.
The IMKB National-100 closed up 28 points, or 1.73 percent at 1,642. Gains totalled 5.7 percent since Monday's 0.06 percent ease on political concerns.
Daily volume fell to 30.2 trillion lira from Wednesday's 36.5 trillion.

"There was selective activity, probably based on profit prospects of companies. Political uncertainty seems to be clearing slowly after the votes which triggers buying," said Okan Alpay from Inter investment.
"There is also no upward move in the dollar or interest rates, so the bourse is still the sole alternative," he added.
Brokers said the market could keep caution ahead of three censure motions filed by opposition parties against the Islamist-led government, scheduled for debate in parliament on February 25 on 26.

Of the 236 shares traded, 107 advanced, 71 declined and 58 closed stable. The IMKB Industrial edged 0.12 percent higher to 1,678, the IMKB Services jumped 3.88 percent to 1,500 and the IMKB Financial gained 3.09 percent to 1,704.

Actives were led by utility Cukurova Elektrik, up 7,500 lira at 217,500, T.Isbank's C series shares, up 2,000 lira at 42,000, car maker Tofas, down 400 lira at 8,200, largely state-owned flat steel giant Eregli, down 250 lira at 21,250 and largely state-owned refiner Tupras, down 3,000 lira at 55,000.
They made up 30.9 percent of the total volume.
